solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Servant followed by worker in ceremony

blocks.note: a page is a boy servant
the worker ant, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A household servant and a labourer taking part together in some formal ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is almost always ANT or BEE in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a grand public show or procession, a kind of ceremony.

clue.text: Bakery — its pies are cooked

indicators.note: cooking something changes it, as the letters are rearranged; 'cook the books' means falsify

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A bakery boasting that every one of its pies is baked on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator and the fodder both belong in the kitchen, so the whole clue reads as a plain description of a bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a shop selling pastries and cakes, a bakery.

clue.text: Actor Clark, good and competent

blocks.note: G = good
able = competent

explanation.surface: A tribute to a film star called Clark as a decent and capable man.
explanation.walkthrough: Clark Gable starred in Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by name: the Hollywood leading man's first name and profession point to his surname.

clue.text: Rain and gales upset Africans

indicators.note: an upset thing is knocked over and out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; 'and' just joins the two words

explanation.surface: Foul weather troubling people in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as a verb about feelings, with the weather as its subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Algerians come from Algeria in North Africa.

clue.text: The car travelling around old country

indicators.note: letters that travel about end up in new places

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

explanation.surface: A car touring an ancient land.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrace was an ancient region of south-east Europe, now split between Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace is a historic region, an old country of the Balkans.

clue.text: Conclusion of prayer beginning to affect soldiers

indicators.note: take the beginning of the next word

blocks.note: first letter of 'affect'
men = soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A prayer ending that is starting to move the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to affect' looks like a verb phrase about soldiers being moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is the word said at the end of a prayer.

clue.text: Residue of something burnt in wood

blocks.note: first definition: the powder left by a fire
second definition: timber from a common broadleaf tree

explanation.surface: The remains of a fire left in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' reads as a forest, but it is the timber, ash.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is what is left after burning, and also the wood of the ash tree.

clue.text: Priest with First in Theology, one holy person favouring best people?

indicators.note: take the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
first letter of 'Theology'
I = one, the Roman numeral
ST = saint

explanation.surface: A cleric with a top degree in divinity who happens to be a saint, and something of a snob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First in Theology' reads as a top degree, but it only gives T. The question mark flags that 'best people' is the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist favours the elite, the supposed best people.

clue.text: Time to join sailor Bill in USA

indicators.note: the first piece is joined by the second

blocks.note: T = time
AB = able seaman

explanation.surface: A moment for a sailor called Bill to sign up in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like the sailor's name; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a restaurant or bar bill a tab.

clue.text: Crazy singer who lacks love for George or Ira?

indicators.note: a crazy arrangement is a jumbled one
the fodder goes without the letter named

blocks.note: anagram fodder
WHO without O (love = zero, from tennis)

explanation.surface: A mad singer who cannot love, wondering whether he is George or Ira.
explanation.walkthrough: George and Ira Gershwin were the brothers who wrote songs such as I Got Rhythm, George the music and Ira the lyrics. The question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the two brothers share the surname, so either first name points to it.

clue.text: Gym apparatus — leap on it Mr Mobile!

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A gym instructor urging an agile man called Mr Mobile to jump on the equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Mobile' reads as a jokey name, which hides the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a piece of gymnastics equipment.

clue.text: Guide farm animal

blocks.note: first definition: to direct the course of something
second definition: a young castrated bull

explanation.surface: Leading a beast around the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are everyday ones: directing a vehicle, and a bullock raised for beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a plain synonym for guide, and the name for a young castrated bull kept on a farm.

clue.text: Discharge with dishonour a bank worker

blocks.note: first definition: to dismiss an officer from the armed forces in disgrace
second definition: someone who pays out and takes in money at a counter

explanation.surface: A bank clerk being sacked in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense, used of military officers, is the less familiar one.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to dismiss dishonourably; a cashier also handles money in a bank.

clue.text: The nerd so wickedly diminished

indicators.note: treated wickedly, the letters are knocked out of shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A geek cruelly belittled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminished' reads as belittled, but it means made shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean made smaller, here specifically in length.

clue.text: More than one lesser actor runs on field

blocks.note: first definition: background players in crowd scenes
second definition: in cricket, runs added to the score that were not hit off the bat, such as byes and wides

explanation.surface: Bit-part players dashing onto a field during filming.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs such as byes and wides added to the score without the batsman hitting the ball. 'Runs' looks like a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras are minor actors, and runs credited in cricket.

clue.text: Pole on ship in the afternoon tucked into hot food

indicators.note: one piece is tucked inside another

blocks.note: toast, served hot
PM = post meridiem, afternoon; goes inside TO|AST

explanation.surface: A sailor in the afternoon eating a hot meal beside the ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' reads as eating, the natural sense with food around.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the upper section of a ship's mast.

clue.text: Some robot to make base component

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words, from the end of 'robot' to the start of 'make'

explanation.surface: Building a robot to make parts for a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Component' reads as a machine part to go with the robot.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the lowest part of anything is its base.

clue.text: Name of woman with bad breath

indicators.note: bad letters are in poor order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

explanation.surface: Identifying a woman who suffers from halitosis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad breath' is such a set phrase that 'bad' does not look like an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one example of a female first name.

clue.text: One’s behind the times — a very tricky situation

blocks.note: one is = I'M, speaking of oneself
passé = out of date

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they are out of date, which is an awkward spot to be in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' means 'one is', which a speaker says as 'I'm'. The accent on passé is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a deadlock from which no progress is possible is a very tricky situation.

clue.text: Time for piece of music

blocks.note: the surface suggests the right moment to play; the setter means time in the musical sense, the speed of the beat
the rate at which a composition is to be played

explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' reads as the moment to play a piece, but it is the musical sense: the pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed of a piece of music, its time in the musician's sense.

clue.text: Wine provided when chap keeps company

blocks.note: chap = man
CO = company; goes inside MA|N

explanation.surface: Wine is laid on whenever a man has guests.
explanation.walkthrough: Mâcon is a Burgundy wine; the accent is dropped in the grid. 'Keeps company' reads as having friends round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a French wine from the Mâconnais in southern Burgundy.

clue.text: Canadian city hotel backed by a poet

blocks.note: H = hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
as printed
John Milton, author of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A hotel in a Canadian city with a poet as its backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed by' here means followed by, not funded by.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: an industrial port city on Lake Ontario, one of several places with this name.

clue.text: Trendy name for pub

blocks.note: in = fashionable
N = name

explanation.surface: Choosing a fashionable name for a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a pub name; 'name' is only its abbreviation, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a traditional public house, often with rooms for travellers.

clue.text: Greek character starts to cherish his independence

indicators.note: take the start of each following word

blocks.note: first letters of Cherish, His, Independence

explanation.surface: A Greek person who values his freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' reads as a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: 'character' means a letter, and this one is the Greek letter written X.

clue.text: Short communication about independent school

indicators.note: turned about, facing the other way

blocks.note: a note is a short message

explanation.surface: A brief message concerning a private school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning'. Eton is a famous English private (fee-paying) school; in Britain 'independent school' means a private one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a well-known independent school.

clue.text: A new poet quite slow in movement

blocks.note: as printed
N = new
Dante, the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A fresh poet whose verse moves along rather sluggishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' reads as motion, but it is also a section of a symphony, where andante is a marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical direction meaning at a moderately slow, walking pace.
